title: Qt: Scroll Filter dialog tree view to new filter
description:
When opening Filter dialog and a new filter is to be created, the new filter is created at the end of the list. If there are a lot of filters, the new one do not apear on the screen. It requires the user to manually scroll down to edit the filter name (which has of course a meaningless default value)

This patch selects the newly created filter in the tree view, so that the user immediately sees where the created filter is. It also scrolls to that index, so that it is always shown.

It should be a general rule to show and to highlight newly created items. I don't know if there are other places where it is not the case.

notes.body: changed the description
Should it also select and scroll here?

As far as I have tested, we cannot select and scroll before having set the model which is done at line 88. These lines (113-116) are inside method `FilterDialog::addFilter` which is private (see filter_dialog.h) and is not called from outside of this class.

Right, these lines are inside the private method, which is always called after line 88, which is inside the constructor. So the model is always set here.

This method is called for instance when clicking on the "+" symbol to add a new filter, which is also a case where scrolling to the new entry might be desired (if editing). The example in the constructor is called when spawning the dialog from for example saving from the bookmarks menu.

Currently, addFilter is always called with start_editing at true, so the row is actually highlighted. I thought edit would also scroll down to the edited row, but it seems not to be the case. So I think we should call scrollTo in every case.

We can add select whenever start_editing is false (default value) just in case some new code will call addFilter with start_editing at false.

Remaining question: shouldn't we have the same behaviour when using "+" and when saving a filter throught bookmark menu (i.e. edit instead of select as proposed in this patch)?

> Currently, addFilter is always called with start_editing at true, so the row is actually highlighted

My experience, at least on some platforms, is that the entire row is not highlighted, only the single index corresponding to the name column.

> shouldn't we have the same behaviour when using "+" and when saving a filter throught bookmark menu

Seems reasonable yes, which is why I suggested it in other comment below. The user probably should edit the filter name when the dialog is launched from the bookmark menu save filter action.

Yep, I'll follow your suggestions of the comments below in the next commit.

Seems that adding and editing does not work properly when called from the constructor. Will only select it for the next commit.

> Seems that adding and editing does not work properly when called from the constructor.

In what way does it not work. Note that you'll have to move the line that sets the item delegate (`ui->filterTreeView->setItemDelegate(new FilterTreeDelegate(this, filter_type));`) before adding the filter if you want editing to work properly.
Yes moving the call to addFilter after setItemDelegate solved the problem.
You could probably set the model before adding the filter, and thus combine the three lines into one check for `if (new_filter_.length() > 0)`. Possibly even end up calling the `addFilter()` member.
The normal behavior for selection in this view is to select rows. Calling `select()` doesn't respect that; should this be `QItemSelectionModel::ClearAndSelect | QItemSelectionModel::Rows)` ?
